subject: Linguistics
title: The Latin Alphabet
description: A 60-second lesson on The Latin Alphabet.

hook.text: You're reading the Latin alphabet right now—it's the most widely used writing system on Earth.

buildup.text: Romans adapted the Greek alphabet via the Etruscans—modifying letters to fit Latin sounds.

discovery.text: The original Latin alphabet had 21 letters; 'J,' 'U,' and 'W' were added much later.

twist.text: Colonial expansion spread the Latin script worldwide—it's now used for languages it was never designed for.

climax.text: Turkish, Vietnamese, and Swahili all adopted Latin letters—with added diacritics for local sounds.

punchline.text: A Roman invention that conquered more territory than Rome ever did.

quiz.question: How did the Latin alphabet spread globally?
